narrative:
The model determined that you have a 43% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability exceeded the bank's acceptance threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the loan amount you requested, the status of your checking account, and your credit history. The requested amount was the single biggest driver, but in your case it actually worked in your favor. At 3,804 DM it was higher than the average of about 3,020 DM among approved applicants, yet the model still viewed the overall size of the request as lowering your risk.

Unfortunately, two other factors pushed strongly in the opposite direction and outweighed that benefit. Your checking account currently shows between 0 and 200 DM, a situation shared by only 18% of approved applicants. Even more influential was your credit history of “no credits or all paid.” This is quite rare—only 1% of approved customers fall into this category—while the large majority (57%) have a history of existing credits that were paid on time. These two elements together signaled higher risk to the model and were the main reasons your application was turned down.

You should focus on building a stronger track record of repaying credit and maintaining a healthier checking-account balance. Once those areas improve, reapply or explore smaller loan amounts that better match your current financial profile.
